correctness.rationale: For x=R^beta, differentiate the exact weighted two-Huff probabilities. The sign equals sign[sqrt(w/(1-w))-(1+lambda*x)/(x+lambda)] in the interior, with the second term increasing strictly from 1 toward lambda. This establishes all three parameter regimes and equality cases including w=0,1. Solving the unique zero and substituting proves the peak. The example reduces exactly to 6*x*x-25*x+22=0 with both solutions x>1; symbolic proof and 5,000 seeded numeric checks were executed from verify_huff.py. The proof, not finite tests, covers the full continuous domain.

value.rationale: In aggregate spatial-demand forecasting, knowing whether the distance-decay coefficient can be learned from total market share is a concrete model-identification issue. The two-district mirrored-distance design is the smallest genuine case mixing demand asymmetry and distance advantage. The result classifies every parameter setting exactly, separates monotone versus nonmonotone decay responses at a sharp demographic threshold, gives the closed-form peak, and constructs two distinct positive exponents explaining the identical measured share. It cautions against assuming one-dimensional fitting is globally unique and motivates collecting district-level shares when the hump region is plausible. It is not a claim about general geographies or optimal retail sites.
